info.title: worker-protocol — grants
info.description: What a Contract's credential covers on this Worker, applied ahead of time by whoever brokered the Contract, and the credential the Worker issues for it. Optional: a Worker that declares no `grants` covers its credentials its own way.

servers.description: GRANT-1. The address the `grants` entry declares, resolved per DESC-36.

address.description: Read from the Worker's Descriptor and resolved per DESC-36. Never assembled by a caller (ENDP-1). The default is `/` and not a host on purpose: a client that was never given an address should fail at its own origin rather than reach somebody else's.

get.description: GRANT-6. A grant belongs to the caller that applied it, and this lists that caller's and no other's — never a credential, which the owner keeps only as a digest.

parameters.name: Worker-Protocol-Capability-Version
parameters.description: ENDP-6. The Capability version the caller expects. A Worker that cannot answer it refuses the request whole with `400` and `unsupported_version`, and never substitutes its own.

parameters.name: traceparent
parameters.description: ENDP-42. W3C Trace Context. The Worker continues the trace this names, in a span of its own, or begins one where the header is absent or cannot be read — and never refuses a request for it. LOG-11: a record written while handling the call carries that trace.

200.description: GRANT-6. This applicant's grants, in the shared page envelope.

Worker-Protocol-Edition.description: ENDP-37. The edition that produced this answer. A caller that sees one it did not expect re-reads the Descriptor rather than parsing the body.

post.description: GRANT-3. The body is the grant's id and the Task types, Actions and event types a credential issued for it covers, each `all` or a list, and optionally `rotate`. Creating issues a credential (GRANT-4); applying again replaces what the grant covers and issues one only when asked to rotate (GRANT-5).

delete.description: GRANT-7. A DELETE, as SUB-9's is (ENDP-36). From the response on, every credential issued for the grant is `401` and every subscription it created has ended (GRANT-9).

parameters.name: grant
parameters.description: GRANT-7. The id of a grant this caller applied. An id it holds no grant under is `404`: ids are unique only beside their applicant, so another's grant under the same id is not this caller's.
